tool.name: dDocent
tool.description: RAD-seq reference assembly and variant calling pipeline
tool.command:
mkdir -p work && cd work &&
## dDocent discovers its input by filename (Locality_Individual.F.fq.gz / .R.fq.gz), ## so the element identifier becomes the sample name. Letters, digits and ## underscores are kept and everything else is replaced by an underscore, so that ## the name is safe in the shell, in dDocent's sed/mawk one-liners and in the ## popmap dDocent writes. #for $element in $reads #set $ident = ''.join([c if (c.isalnum() or c == '_') else '_' for c in str($element.element_identifier)]) #if $element.forward.ext == 'fastqsanger.gz' ln -s '$element.forward' '${ident}.F.fq.gz' && ln -s '$element.reverse' '${ident}.R.fq.gz' && #else gzip -c '$element.forward' > '${ident}.F.fq.gz' && gzip -c '$element.reverse' > '${ident}.R.fq.gz' && #end if #end for
## dDocent derives the population of a sample from the part of its name before the ## first underscore and refuses to run when there is none for f in *.F.fq.gz; do case "\$f" in *_*) ;; *) echo "ERROR: collection element '\${f%.F.fq.gz}' does not follow the dDocent naming convention Locality_Individual (no underscore in the name)." >&2; exit 1 ;; esac; done &&
#if $analysis.analysis_type == 'assembly_only' and $reference_source.reference_option == 'history' echo "ERROR: 'Build the reference only' cannot be combined with 'Use a reference from the history' - choose one, or extend the analysis to mapping." >&2; exit 1 && #end if
#if $popmap_source.popmap_option == 'file' cp '$popmap_source.popmap_file' popmap && #end if
#if $reference_source.reference_option == 'history' cp '$reference_source.reference_file' reference.fasta && #end if
## dDocent rejects NUMProc < 2 and its configuration parser is strictly ## positional, so the configuration file is written as a pair of lines per option NUMProc=\$(( \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-4} < 2 ? 2 : \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-4} )); MAXMEM=\$(( \${GALAXY_MEMORY_MB:-8192} / 1024 ));
#if $reference_source.reference_option == 'denovo' ASSEMBLY=yes; ATYPEP=$reference_source.atype; SIM=$reference_source.sim; K1=$reference_source.k1; K2=$reference_source.k2; #else ## not read by dDocent when no assembly is requested, but the parser needs a value ASSEMBLY=no; ATYPEP=PE; SIM=0.9; K1=5; K2=6; #end if
#if $analysis.analysis_type == 'snps' MAPV=yes; SNPV=yes; #elif $analysis.analysis_type == 'map_only' MAPV=yes; SNPV=no; #else MAPV=no; SNPV=no; #end if
printf 'Number of Processors
%s
Maximum Memory
%s
Trimming
yes
Assembly?
%s
Type_of_Assembly
%s
Clustering_Similarity%%
%s
Minimum within individual coverage level to include a read for assembly (K1)
%s
Minimum number of individuals a read must be present in to include for assembly (K2)
%s
Mapping_Reads?
%s
Mapping_Match_Value
%s
Mapping_MisMatch_Value
%s
Mapping_GapOpen_Penalty
%s
Calling_SNPs?
%s
Email
galaxy@galaxyproject.org
' "\$NUMProc" "\$MAXMEM" "\$ASSEMBLY" "\$ATYPEP" "\$SIM" "\$K1" "\$K2" "\$MAPV" '$mapping.match' '$mapping.mismatch' '$mapping.gap' "\$SNPV" > Configuration &&
## dDocent reads all further input from the configuration file; stdin is closed so ## that an unforeseen prompt fails instead of hanging the job failed=0 && dDocent Configuration < /dev/null || { echo "ERROR: dDocent exited with a non-zero status." >&2; failed=1; };
## dDocent prints most in-pipeline failures on stdout and still exits 0, so the ## outputs have to be validated here instead of relying on its exit status #if $reference_source.reference_option == 'denovo' [ -s reference.fasta ] || { echo "ERROR: dDocent did not produce an assembly - reference.fasta is missing or empty." >&2; failed=1; }; #end if if [ "\$MAPV" = yes ]; then for bam in *-RG.bam; do [ -e "\$bam" ] || continue; [ -s "\$bam" ] || { echo "ERROR: BAM file '\$bam' is empty, so the reads of that sample could not be mapped." >&2; failed=1; }; done; true; fi; if [ "\$SNPV" = yes ]; then [ -s Final.recode.vcf ] && [ "\$(grep -vc '^#' Final.recode.vcf)" -gt 0 ] || { echo "ERROR: no variant was called - Final.recode.vcf is missing, empty or contains no records." >&2; failed=1; }; fi; ## the fastp and samtools logs are the only place where a sample with broken input ## shows up: dDocent itself only greps the BAM logs for 'error', and fastp reports ## truncated or mismatched read pairs as "WARNNIG: different read numbers" (sic) ## and then silently drops the unmatched reads. if [ -d logfiles ]; then for log in logfiles/*.trim.log logfiles/*.bam.log; do [ -e "\$log" ] || continue; grep -qE '(^|: )ERROR|fail(ed)? to |different read numbers' "\$log" && { echo "ERROR: dDocent reported a problem in '\$log':" >&2; grep -E '(^|: )ERROR|fail(ed)? to |different read numbers' "\$log" >&2; failed=1; }; done; true; fi;
## expose the trimmed reads for 'dDocent Remake Reference' and further analyses; ## dDocent writes .R1.fq.gz for both layouts and .R2.fq.gz only for paired data mkdir -p trimmed_reads trimmed_reads_se; for f in *.R1.fq.gz; do [ -e "\$f" ] || continue; sample="\${f%.R1.fq.gz}"; if [ -e "\$sample.R2.fq.gz" ]; then ln -L "\$f" "trimmed_reads/\$sample.forward.fq.gz" || cp "\$f" "trimmed_reads/\$sample.forward.fq.gz"; ln -L "\$sample.R2.fq.gz" "trimmed_reads/\$sample.reverse.fq.gz" || cp "\$sample.R2.fq.gz" "trimmed_reads/\$sample.reverse.fq.gz"; else ln -L "\$f" "trimmed_reads_se/\$sample.fq.gz" || cp "\$f" "trimmed_reads_se/\$sample.fq.gz"; fi; done; ## an empty collection would break the dataset discovery of the other output rmdir trimmed_reads 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir trimmed_reads_se 2>/dev/null || true; mkdir -p logfiles; [ -e dDocent_main.LOG ] || : > dDocent_main.LOG; tar -czf dDocent_logs.tar.gz logfiles dDocent_main.LOG; [ "\$failed" -eq 0 ] || { echo "---- last lines of the dDocent summary logs ----" >&2; for log in logfiles/*.log; do case "\$log" in logfiles/bwa.*.log|logfiles/*.trim.log|logfiles/*.bam.log) continue ;; esac; echo "== \$log ==" >&2; tail -n 3 "\$log" >&2; done; echo "ERROR: dDocent did not finish successfully, see the messages above." >&2; exit 1; }

param.name: reads
param.label: Raw paired-end reads
param.help: A list of paired collections, one per individual. dDocent only accepts gzipped FASTQ, uncompressed fastqsanger is gzipped by the wrapper. The element identifiers become the sample names, see the help section below.

param.name: popmap_option
param.label: Population assignment
param.help: A popmap maps every sample to a population. dDocent needs it for the FreeBayes '--populations' option.
param.option: Infer from the sample names (prefix before the first underscore)
Use a popmap from the history

param.name: popmap_file
param.label: Popmap
param.help: Two tab-separated columns, sample name and population, one line per sample.

param.name: reference_option
param.label: Reference
param.help: dDocent either builds a reference de novo from the reads (the default for RAD-seq without a genome assembly) or maps the reads against a reference provided in the history.
param.option: Build a de novo reference (Rainbow + CD-HIT)
Use a reference from the history

param.name: reference_file
param.label: Reference genome or contigs
param.help: dDocent maps to a file called reference.fasta, which the wrapper creates for you. The contig headers must not contain whitespace.

param.name: analysis_type
param.label: Analysis steps
param.help: dDocent always trims the reads; the remaining stages can be limited to the reference assembly or the mapping step.
param.option: Map the reads and call variants
Map the reads only (no variant calling)

section.name: mapping
section.title: Read mapping and variant calling options

data.name: final_vcf
data.label: ${tool.name} on ${on_string}: variants called in at least 90% of the individuals

tool.help:
.. class:: infomark
**What it does**
`dDocent <https://www.ddocent.com/>`_ chains established tools into a single RAD-seq pipeline for non-model organisms, following the workflow of Puritz et al. 2014 (doi:10.7717/peerj.431):
1. **Trimming** - ``fastp`` removes adapters and low-quality bases from every individual, and infers the minimum read length from the data. 2. **De novo reference assembly** (optional) - reads are assembled per individual with ``Rainbow``, filtered for within-individual coverage (K1) and for presence across individuals (K2), and clustered with ``CD-HIT`` at the requested similarity into ``reference.fasta``. Skip this step by providing a reference from the history instead. 3. **Mapping** - ``BWA-MEM`` maps the trimmed reads to the reference with the configured match/mismatch/gap scores, and ``samtools`` adds a read group to every alignment. 4. **Variant calling** - ``FreeBayes`` is run in parallel over the intervals covered by the reads, the per-instance calls are merged with ``vcfcombine``, and ``vcftools`` retains the sites genotyped in at least 90% of the individuals (``Final.recode.vcf``).
@HELP_SAMPLE_NAMING@
---
.. class:: warningmark
**Reads must be paired**
dDocent only accepts ``*.fq.gz`` input, so uncompressed ``fastqsanger`` elements are gzipped by the wrapper. Every element of the input collection must contain both a forward and a reverse read file. Reads demultiplexed with **Stacks: process radtags** are the usual input; relabel the resulting collection so that the element identifiers follow the ``Locality_Individual`` convention before running dDocent.
---
.. class:: infomark
**Choosing assembly parameters**
K1, K2 and the CD-HIT similarity strongly affect the number of reference contigs and therefore the number of RAD loci that can be genotyped. dDocent ships two survey scripts, ``ReferenceOpt.sh`` and ``RefMapOpt.sh``, that sweep these parameters by running the assembly many times (hundreds of assemblies for a typical range). They are shell-command tools driven by follow-up plotting and human judgement of the plateau, so they are not wrapped here; run them outside Galaxy, then enter the chosen values. ``dDocent Remake Reference`` re-assembles the reference from already-trimmed reads for a single parameter set.
Sensible starting points for a small ddRAD data set are K1 = 5, K2 = 10% of the individuals, and a CD-HIT similarity of 0.9.
---
.. class:: infomark
**Outputs**
* ``reference`` - the assembled contigs, or the reference that was mapped against * ``trimmed reads`` - one paired collection per individual, the input of ``dDocent Remake Reference`` * ``read groups (BAM)`` and ``covered intervals`` - per-sample alignments and the genomic intervals covered by at least one read, the input of ``FreeBayes`` * ``raw variants`` - the merged FreeBayes output before filtering, ``variants called in at least 90% of the individuals`` - the recommended starting point for ``dDocent Filters``, whose output can be fed to ``dDocent Error Count`` * ``popmap used`` - the sample to population assignment that was applied * ``parameters used`` - the settings of the run, as recorded by dDocent * ``fastp trimming reports`` and ``logs`` - per-sample QC and the full log archive
If a stage fails, dDocent still terminates with exit status 0 and prints "dDocent has finished with an analysis"; the wrapper therefore inspects the reference, the BAM files, the VCF, and the per-sample logs, and fails the job with a pointer to the offending log instead of handing back empty results.
